label: Street's dilemma extended to epistemic reasons: realist self-application and survivors
summary: #1585, revised after the independent semantic challenge on PR #1611. Source: in the pinned Street 2006 witness, n. 2 (p. 156) and n. 57 (pp. 163–164) say she thinks the dilemma extends to realism about epistemic reasons, without argument, and that her alien-investigator reply assumes shared judgments about epistemic reasons, a complication she leaves undiscussed. Two stating claims record this. Her first horn (pp. 121–122, the Bermuda analogy) holds the realist's truths fixed and lets the judgments vary with selective pressure, then argues by a coincidence step that the actual judgments are in all likelihood off track. Analyst reconstruction, attribution deferred. A Darwinian profile for one scoped epistemic evaluative judgment separates origin fixing, tracking failure, actual inaccuracy, justified defeat (undercutting in the existing ReliabilityFrame) and global epistemic nihilism. Verified results: (1) cross-history horn (28051e37): constant correctness and a verdict varying across histories give an incorrect verdict in some scenario; the probabilistic step to actual error is not derived; its controls (641cb6d7) give a fixed-truth case with an accurate actual verdict and no within-history failure. (2) Within-history-variation variant (8be398bc), an analyst reading that is not Street's horn and that her paradigm constant-correctness realism fails: origin fixing and within-history variation of correctness give a tracking failure among scenarios with the actual history. (3) Self-application (60425b3c): under a uniform mismatch-undercuts policy, the variant's premises for the debunker's own epistemic basis, sole-basis dependence and warrant-needs-undefeated-support give lack of warrant for the debunking conclusion, reusing undercutSoleBasisPrecludesWarrant; this is self-undermining, not self-refutation. The policy also treats an actually false verdict as undercutting (the actual scenario is a history-mate), so it does not by itself separate actual inaccuracy from justified defeat. (4) History-fixed correctness with actual accuracy keeps every history-mate accurate (6e78b91c). (5) Controls (92a88754): one omission example shows origin fixing is needed; the self-application premises are jointly satisfiable with the conclusion true and thin F6 intact; a no-undercutting model with history-fixed correctness keeps warrant, which shows consistency, not that antirealism specifically secures warrant. Surviving replies to this reconstruction: constructivism and functional accounts, whose correctness is fixed by the history. Necessitarian realism is NOT a survivor: it fails the within-history premise, but it is the paradigm target of the cross-history horn and survives result 4 only if its actual verdicts are accurate, which the horn disputes. Relation-asserting supervenience realism belongs to Street's second horn, which is not formalized here. The independent-basis (alien) reply against sole-basis dependence remains open for epistemic reasons. Frontier delta: no change. Root connection: F6 is a floor item that these results neither use nor threaten; the route to the case needs the unbuilt #930 bridge from epistemic warrant to acceptance of root-route premises.
blocker: Open: the probabilistic coincidence step from cross-history mismatch to likely actual error (which needs a measure over histories and verdicts); a defeat principle that triggers on cross-history mismatch without counting bare actual falsity as defeat, which is needed before the self-application can use Street's own horn rather than the within-history variant; Street's second horn against relation-asserting realism; whether any actual epistemic judgment meets either reading; sole-basis dependence of the debunking conclusion; and the #930 bridge. Next test: give a finite measure over histories and state the coincidence step as a bound on the probability of actual accuracy under constant correctness and history-driven verdicts.
